100: And there is no difference in this issur as to whether he tells people who are not relatives of the man [spoken of] or his relatives. And even for one to speak about his brother before his father is lashon hara. Even if he intends by his telling that his relatives reprove him for this, it is also forbidden. For he should have reproved him first by himself and not immediately gone to speak his shame — unless he assumed that his reproof would be of no avail, in which case it is permitted.
